The five new 2026-10-05 mappings are each a narrow proxy for one declared endpoint: paired criteria-version reclassification is not accuracy or review time (Benet-Pages t2/t3); tool-vs-tool agreement on conflicting variants is not accuracy against ground truth (So 2024); agreement with ClinGen eRepo submissions from an unreviewed, not-peer-reviewed preprint is not independent accuracy (HECTOR); and BRCA2 exon 15-26 functional-data classification yield is not a complete professional classification review (Hu 2026). None implies qualified human scientific review or Rewire model execution.

The 2026-10-07 Figure S10 Panel B mapping is a single conventional classifier's (SVMrejection) coverage/rejection-rate baseline across nine inter-dataset train-test combinations (cross-dataset, cross-species where applicable). VISp and ALM share GSE115746. MTG is a separate human single-nucleus dataset; combinations involving MTG include cross-species data. Some two-dataset training combinations still share the mouse study with the test dataset, so independent-study holdout must not be inferred for all nine combinations. It is NOT a known-type accuracy claim, NOT an unknown/absent-type-detection accuracy claim, and NOT a claim that SVMrejection outperforms or underperforms any other classifier. The scored denominator for each individual train-test experiment is UNREPORTED in the retrieved main text and supplement; Table 2's raw per-dataset cell counts (VISp 12,832; ALM 8,758; MTG 14,636) are recorded as context only on the three new dataset records, not as a confirmed denominator. metric_direction is "unknown" for all nine results, for the same reason already established for the Baron Human unlabeled-percentage results. Only the SVMrejection row (one of 18 classifiers shown in the source figure, nine train-test values) and only the 34-population annotation level (Figure S10 Panel B, not Panel A) are ingested; the other 17 classifiers and Figure S10 Panel A remain unextracted. Figure S9 (PBMC) is not part of this mapping: Panel A carries no printed digit labels at any resolution checked and separately shows an unresolved conflict between its own caption text, the page's single legend, and the figure's overall title over which metric it displays; Panel B is a different, non-transfer endpoint (prior-knowledge classifiers applied directly, no training performed within that evaluation). This mapping predates and does not evaluate scTab, CellTypist, Azimuth, scANVI or scParadise, and does not measure or substitute for the common-protocol cross-study benchmark gap tracked separately at rewire-benchmarks #27. use-case-cell-type-annotation-transfer remains an incomplete, open evidence-collection case; its collection_plan.status and evidence_gaps are unchanged by this addition.

The 2026-10-07 CIViC-Fact v3 mapping for use-case-egfr-nsclc-actionability-resistance-evidence is a single post-cutoff temporal cohort (2026-03-03 to 2026-06-09) scored under two retriever configurations, not two independent cohorts and not an independent replication. It is pan-cancer: no EGFR- or NSCLC-specific subgroup, score, or clinical efficacy result is present. It is within-linked-publication passage retrieval (the source paper for each claim is already known via CIViC's existing link), not an open-corpus literature-search or citation-context benchmark, and does not establish performance for finding appropriate studies across a clinical corpus. Coverage is partial and the cohort is enriched: only 40 of the original 150 candidate CIViC entries are scored, and the source's own Discussion states this cohort is not representative of CIViC overall. Uncertainty is unreported for this endpoint and no confidence interval is recomputed. Table 2's evidence-retrieval entry/document counts (907/99/88 CIViC entries) and the Methods-stated retrieval-subset example counts (n_train=3456/n_dev=1194/n_test=1120) are different units from the same source; this addition does not resolve that apparent discrepancy by inference and does not ingest either figure. This mapping does not close the benchmark-execution gap tracked separately at rewire-benchmarks #28. Reviewer count, blinding and replicate/seed structure for the manual retrieval-success judgment (37/40, 92.5%) are unreported in the source and are not assumed; this is distinct from the source's separately described curator/group-consensus process for cohort reference-label assignment. The two Huggingface model identifiers (ncbi/MedCPT-Cross-Encoder; Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-8B), confirmed via Table 4, are namespace identifiers only, not pinned immutable checkpoint revisions; none is reported by the source. Repository-root GitHub licence metadata is null and no root LICENSE file exists, but a nested data_builder/LICENSE (GPLv3, 29 June 2007) exists at pinned commit 1a767d889b015a836f0f4331afcac5cef165ec7f; its scope over the full dataset, trained models, or other repository components is unestablished and not assumed, separate from the article's own CC-BY-4.0; no code/data/model copies were ingested. use-case-egfr-nsclc-actionability-resistance-evidence remains an incomplete, open evidence-collection case; its collection_plan.status and evidence_gaps are unchanged by this addition.

The 2026-10-07 PertEval-scFM mapping for use-case-genetic-perturbation-response is a single table's three configurations (GEARS, MLP baseline, Mean baseline) from one paper's Norman single-gene, 2,000-HVG, SPECTRA-sparsification AUSPC protocol, scoring the perturbation-effect delta=P-Xc (Eq. 5), not raw post-perturbation expression. It is an expression-change-prediction proxy, the same proxy class as the existing GEARS Supplementary Table 6 mappings; it does not establish prospective experiment-selection hit rate (case 6's separate endpoint) and must not be merged, averaged or combined with Table 6's values (different gene universe, split mechanism and metric). GEARS here is an independent from-scratch training run by this paper's authors (official implementation, only the train-test split modified, no pretrained weights), not the original GEARS authors' own Table 6 checkpoint/run. AUSPC's printed +/- is the source's own propagated standard error (Appendix F.2 formula, attributed to triplicate experiments per Appendix I's Figure I1 caption; main-text Figure 2 caption uses the same 'standard error' wording) -- an author-reported quantity, not an independently resampled model-seed standard deviation or confidence interval, and its mathematical derivation is not independently validated here. Figure I1's caption states '8 train-test splits' against Table 1's seven S-columns; this is preserved as printed, not resolved. The Mean baseline's input population ('all cells in the same context') is not fully specified by the source as control-only or training-only; an independently pinned code observation (commit ce48c8b998901c8f8b6275114caac3a4d8543c0b) is kept as a separate, dated fact, not merged with the paper's definition, and that commit's correspondence to the published run is unverified. Input budgets differ across the three configurations. Per-sparsification-split (S0.1-S0.7) scored perturbation counts are not printed by the source and are not computed or inferred. use-case-genetic-perturbation-response remains an incomplete, open evidence-collection case; a confirmed, directly relevant 27-method/29-dataset benchmark (scPerturBench, Wei et al., Nat. Methods) remains genuinely paywalled and unread. This mapping does not close the focused execution gap tracked at rewire-benchmarks #29 (a frozen, matched Norman control panel with a metric-sensitivity check and a separately registered context-transfer protocol).
